meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now show me what you're basing the zero on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend; pasting a finished draft into a new file proves nothing about who wrote it.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his file, and nobody in that classroom hears a word about it.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line of Shakespeare is a citation error, Hale, not proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. So what are you putting on the table?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, that's called thinking. I asked what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Then he'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him and nothing more. Private, before December 1, the zero gone and his file untouched, and I want all of that from you in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Put Thursday in your email, and I'll confirm it with Owen tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school and not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require all of this confirmed in writing. You said you would send that tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12 with nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times and then answering her pasting defence with an offer to look at any dated earlier draft, because it was specific, dated and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Bringing out the outline after she had asked what you were proposing, because it read as a dodge and made her sharper rather than moving her.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, which came very close to that memory, though it proves nothing about the essay and is only why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you were putting on the table after the quotation, answer right then with the 4.4 rewrite instead of adding the outline.
